source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: State and prove the work-energy theorem for a constant force.
questions.solution:
**Work-energy theorem:** The work done by the net force on a body equals the change in its kinetic energy.

Proof: Let a constant force F act on mass m, producing acceleration a. From v² = u² + 2as:

W = F·s = (ma)s = m(a·s). Since as = (v² − u²)/2,

W = m(v² − u²)/2 = ½mv² − ½mu² = ΔKE.

Thus work done = change in kinetic energy. Proved.
questions.knowledgeNote: The theorem holds for ALL forces — conservative and non-conservative alike.

questions.question: An electric motor has a power output of 2 kW. How much time will it take to lift a 500 kg mass through 20 m? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.knowledgeNote: Power = Work/Time; 1 W = 1 J/s and 1 HP = 746 W.

questions.question: Calculate the work done in stretching a spring of force constant 200 N/m by 0.1 m from its unstretched position.
questions.solution:
Work stored as elastic potential energy: W = ½kx².

W = ½ × 200 × (0.1)² = 100 × 0.01 = **1 J**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Spring work goes as x² — doubling the stretch quadruples the stored energy.

questions.question: Show that the total mechanical energy of a freely falling body is conserved (neglect air resistance).
questions.solution:
Drop mass m from height H. At height h with velocity v, energy conservation from rest gives v² = 2g(H − h).

KE + PE = ½mv² + mgh = ½m·2g(H − h) + mgh = mgH − mgh + mgh = **mgH = constant**.

At the top (h = H) it is all potential; at the ground (h = 0) it is all kinetic — the sum never changes.
questions.knowledgeNote: Only conservative forces (gravity, spring) conserve mechanical energy; friction converts part of it to heat.

questions.question: A car of mass 1000 kg moves at a uniform speed of 20 m/s against a total resistive force of 500 N. What power must the engine develop?
questions.solution:
At uniform speed the driving force equals the resistance: F = 500 N.

P = F·v = 500 × 20 = 10,000 W = **10 kW**.
questions.knowledgeNote: For steady motion P = Fv — the same form as W = F·s divided by time.

questions.question: Define the kilowatt-hour (kWh). How many joules are equal to 1 kWh?
questions.solution:
**1 kWh** is the energy consumed by a 1 kW appliance running for 1 hour (the commercial 'unit' of electrical energy).

1 kWh = 1000 W × 3600 s = **3.6 × 10⁶ J**.
questions.knowledgeNote: kWh is a unit of ENERGY, not power — a classic one-mark NEB trap.
